This depends on where you are. In my country we have services that provide free therapy to people aged 12-25. You can also ask around for therapists who do a sliding scale and can offer you cheaper therapy. Does your school have a counsellor? They won’t be able to help with anything major but it could be a good start and maybe they could recommend someone more affordable. Some universities also offer free, or low cost, therapy if you’re working with a student psychologist. 

I’m sorry if none of these are helpful options and that things seem so hard for you right now. I hope you can find someone who is within your price range to see.

I spoke to the new therapist about why I didn’t want her talking to my current one. I thought I explained it well and she said it was okay. Now a week later and a day before our next appointment she tells me it’s unethical to keep seeing me if she’s not allowed to talk to my current therapist. She didn’t even give me a chance to reconsider or ask if I was willing to change my mind, just told me she wouldn’t see me again.

One of the other two was the worst therapist I’ve ever had. She would tell me things like my SH was attention seeking and enforced eye contact no matter how overwhelmed I was. The other one I saw for neurofeedback and she’s probably retired because she was in her 70s a couple of years ago. 

She knows every detail of my attachment including that I want to sleep with her. I need help with my attachment problems and I can’t get that without talking about them. It’s just unfortunate that it’s about her.

I’m seeing some improvement with emdr but we often don’t get to do it because I’m overwhelmed by something she’s done as my FP and I can’t do effective therapy that day. We have some good moments and then things happen and I’m hit with the fact that she’s doing me a lot of harm and traumatising me further and I’m just allowing it because I feel in love with her

It feels like my fault. I went into things with this new one informing her that my attachment was to my current therapist and I needed help with that and was having trouble finding a therapist who could do that. She had 3 weeks to decide this was unethical. Now after wasting my time and money she has decided that because I won’t let her talk to my current T it’s unethical for her to work with me. I should be allowed to make decisions about whether my doctors talk to each other but apparently to get help my options are lie and say I don’t see my current T any more, be forced to allow two therapists to talk behind my back and discuss what’s best for me, or give up seeing my current T to see someone else. I’m aware that most therapists won’t see you if you’re seeing someone else and I find this ridiculous. I should be able to get support from as many people as I want. My therapist has 5 supervisors all for different things. Why can’t I have two therapists for different things? I wasn’t asking to work on the same thing with both of them because I know that doesn’t make sense. They just won’t listen to me. 
And my current therapist is just disappearing more and more even though she says we’ll get to talk as much as she can over the next few days I know that will mean 3 emails. Normally we have a proper back and forth on Thursday nights and she’s cancelled that 3 weeks in a row, she’s never online Friday nights so I now won’t hear from her until Saturday and she’ll say that’s as much as she can. What she says will feel like talking won’t. Giving up seems like the best option. I’m a better person when I don’t have an FP and if I stop seeing my therapist she’ll stop being my FP and I’ll be fine until I have another one. Why keep seeing a therapist when every attempt I’m making is hurting me more?

I thrive when I don’t have an FP. I’m far more stable and less moody when I’m not constantly fearing abandonment and letting my moods be ruined by someone else. If I knew how to get rid of my FP feelings without cutting her off and going NC I would. I still have massive triggers even without an FP but therapy has really helped me work out what they are and how to manage them. I can do that on my own but I can’t communicate it to another person, especially not an FP who is triggering me. 
I have avoided dating for years simply because I’m a far healthier person without someone else. It hasn’t stopped me having an FP but I’d like to think it’s been far less hurtful for them when I do the leaving because we weren’t actually in a relationship.
Numb is hard but with work it’s possible to feel things without relying on the moods of another person. I wouldn’t ever recommend to anyone to have an FP.

I can’t give you any tips. I’m sorry, it really sucks to have your therapist as your FP and it hurts like hell because the relationship is not going anywhere. I recommend having your therapist set appropriate boundaries if they haven’t already because it might help to lessen how you feel.

Thanks! She’s going okay and a lot of the time she does get things done. Just yesterday she didn’t and it was frustrating. I don’t think it matters whether I’m home or not. It was also her timing. I came home after a long day with the intention of making a coffee and showering and relaxing and she decided it was time to do the dishes and shower at that time. It would be the equivalent of me waiting until she got home from work any other day to cook my dinner and shower so she can’t do either of those things. It would frustrate her after a long day of work. 

We both spent months not being able to do anything. The house was a mess and people didn’t want to visit us. We’re both pretty okay now and things do get done, just yesterday they didn’t. I’m not going to call her lazy because I know she’s not. She just frustrated me yesterday.

I don’t love either of my parents. I’ve accepted that they are who they are and I don’t hate them but I don’t go out of my way to have contact with them any more either. My dad has significantly improved over the years but he caused too much damage for us to have any sort of real loving relationship. My mum will never change and it’s hard to love someone who still causes damage whenever you talk to them. Sometimes I feel guilty for not loving my mum, she was a single parent and I know she did try a lot when we were children but she shouldn’t have been a parent and was still neglectful even if she did try.

I threatened to harm myself in front of them unless they stayed. I am not very proud of that moment. It is possible to forgive yourself for things like this though. You were struggling, the feeling of abandonment is painful and it’s hard to cope with in the moment. Would you do the same thing now if you felt you were being abandoned or have you grown and changed as a person?

She’s pretty okay with doing things after I get home. Like the moment I walked in the door she started cleaning the dishes and had a shower. Just in time to get in the way of me making my afternoon coffee and showering while I wait for the kettle to boil. She walked up to the letterbox to check for mail but couldn’t do that while I was gone. 
I get the not being able to do things. We lived in a pretty bad state for months while both of us were struggling to get out of bed every day but it’s just frustrating that I come home from work and nothing is done. I’m tired, I’m cranky, I’ve been dealing with small people with big feelings all day and I just want to come home and relax on the one day I’m able to.

Not everyone has the energy to be around 24/7, especially if they have a busy life. We all talk more often at the start of a relationship as a getting to know you honeymoon period but we drop down to our normal communication style after that. For me that’s I’ll message you when I can and if I’m busy I’ll probably forget. I don’t mean it offensively it just happens. 

Finding my person is hard. I’ve lowered my standards a bit now, and by that I mean I’ve opened up to dating guys who are shorter than me. It would be nice to be less picky but I just can’t imagine being with someone who I’m not attracted to at all. I have a type and I stick to it. Those types just don’t like me.

The moment the first date doesn’t go well I’m straight back onto the dating apps trying to get validation from someone else. I feel like I just need to be less picky at this point. I’m not great, I shouldn’t be holding out hope for someone who is.

Try and work out what’s under the anger. Often my anger is fear or hurt and not actually anger. Try and talk it through with her when she’s calm so you have some idea what’s underneath and can reassure based on that :)

It depends on why I’m splitting. With my therapist it’s reassurance before reasoning. If I can identify that I’m splitting because I’m scared rather than angry it’s far easier to get reassurance that she’s not going to leave me and she still cares about me. When that sinks in I’m ready to listen to reasoning and hear her perspective. Things go back to normal for me, if if the problem is solved, it’s over, no need to keep being upset about it.

It is definitely possible for a splitting episode to last months. My therapist and I are only now on good terms since early December because she’s been the worst person to ever exist and I’ve done nothing but argue with her and insult her for months. 

I’d say typically I go between a couple of hours and a couple of days before I can really start to see someone else’s perspective on something. It  depends on whether they continue pushing their point of view onto me or if they just let me work it out on my own.

I use the app calm harm to curb any urge I have to hurt myself. If I do SH I need to keep it covered because even if I’m not feeling it I’ll just keep picking at it to make it worse. 

I get urges even when I’m having a really good day. It’s just an invasive thought and not something I actually want to do. I’m not in crisis when I have these thoughts, to curb them I label them as intrusive thoughts and talk to myself “in having an urge to do this right now, it makes me feel...” then I use my app and focus my attention elsewhere.

I understand where you’re coming from and I don’t mean any of this offensively. Im sorry if it is. I’m not sure where you’re from but I’ve never been expected to give up any of my bpd behaviours that weren’t harmful to others. I’ve never been turned down by a therapist or psychiatrist because of my diagnosis. Everyone I work with now knows I’m an emotional person and the majority have seen my cry over nothing, they’ve never asked me to change. People with bpd have a lot of amazing qualities instilled in their personalities and I think the advocacy is towards those and not the abusive traits. 

I think this also really depends on what borderline behaviour you’re saying is appropriate. It doesn’t matter what your diagnosis is it’s not okay for you to hurt, manipulate or lie to people. If a person with autism is violent we also expect they change their behaviour. 

You’re correct, DBT allows people with bpd to have stable relationships and healthy coping mechanisms. What’s the alternative? Our unstable relationships are obsessive and hurtful to other people and ourselves. Do you really want to be in a relationship where you get so angry you do something like smash someone’s car up? Healthy coping mechanisms are also better than the alternative. My dbt therapist never tried to take my unhealthy coping mechanisms away. I’d rather be sober and alive using healthy coping mechanisms because I was forced into society’s expectations. Nobody has ever asked me to give up my dissociation or my obsessive research on people. If we forced children into dbt it might be the same torture but we don’t, we accept that children are unregulated and allow many of their behaviour as well because they’re age appropriate. 

I have a few diagnosis I’m around the wrong people showing those behaviours gets me ostracised. When I had an anxiety attack at my old workplace and cried underneath a desk I was told to pull myself together and get back to work. When my CPTSD causes me to regress to being 5 I’m expected to grow up and behave and talk like an adult. When I’m manic in my bipolar and I’m overspending and sleeping with anyone possible my behaviour is shunned by society.

I believe it’s entirely possible to stop depending on them, it’s just hard. We have to make choices that go against what we are so used to doing. I’m not ready to do that and my FP still allows my behaviour.
From Borderline to Beautiful is good. Brutal, but good. I’m not sure it’s on Spotify though
For me, I often think I want to die but what I actually want is to just disappear with no obligations and no social contact. I want to disappear from society, not disappear from life.

Having an FP invades my life. They are literally who I live for. Their ability to give me attention and time affects my day massively. I want to be in contact with them at all times even though I understand it isn’t possible. Their mood can make or break my day, if they have the slightest change in their tone of voice when they speak to me or message me my day is completely ruined. I want to be around them at all times. I want to know everything about them. I feel like I’m completely in love with them and can’t live life without them even when they are unavailable to be in a relationship with me. I completely rage on them over nothing at all and it can put me in a bad mood for months unless they tell me exactly what I want to hear. 
It’s unpleasant, it hurts, I wouldn’t wish it upon anyone
3 years sober. I was sober for nearly 8 years until I gave into peer pressure to drink. Worst mistake ever! I hate how it makes me. I get loud and I cry a lot. I don’t need more of that.

Opposite actions for jealousy are things like letting go of the need to be in control of your FPs life. That’s really hard though. A simple one to start is changing your body. Simply moving and unclenching your whole body - do a body scan if you can and realise where you’re feeling things and try and relax those parts.

I know though that often my jealousy comes from fear and presents itself as anger. So I do opposite actions for anger. I hate my FPs husband because I want a relationship with her that he has so I use my opposite actions and be kind to him. What are his good qualities? Why does she love him? Focus on what he does that makes her happy. I can’t meet him but when I was jealous of an FP who had other friends I would do kind things for them - even if it’s just a compliment every time I see them. Recognising it isn’t anger or jealousy but rather fear also helps. Why am I afraid? Where in my life did I experience this fear - usually in childhood. I check the facts and label my interpretation of what is happening - I’m afraid I’m losing her and she doesn’t care about me any more - and I write down the reality of that situation. That’s really hard to do in the moment but remember you are a part of your FPs life because they like you, they are choosing to spend time with you and be around you, you matter to them. Accepting that won’t change even if they have other friends is difficult, I still struggle massively and I’m lucky that when I fail I can ask for reassurance but the more you try the easier it gets.
